title: Compact Command Rail: progressive disclosure and route clustering for multi-workspace consoles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Redesign the left navigation to reduce noise and speed up context switching across workspaces while exposing high-value console surfaces (dashboards, rollouts, cost views). Deliver a compact, keyboard-first command rail that clusters related routes, supports lightweight previews (mini-dashboard cards), and preserves quick workspace switching without deeply nesting routes.
problem_statement: Our current console left rail has grown organically: many top-level items, inconsistent grouping, and heavy visual weight. Engineers and platform teams report friction when switching workspaces or jumping to rollout/cost views. This ticket proposes an IA pattern ("compact command rail") that balances discoverability and density for power users.
goals: Reduce average route selection time by 20% for power workflows (dashboards, rollouts, cost views)
Make workspace switching available with one keyboard stroke and visible at top of rail
Enable in-rail lightweight previews for Rollouts and Cost to avoid full route loads for quick checks
Keep the console accessible (ARIA + keyboard) and support progressive disclosure for infrequent routes
proposed_solution: Introduce a compact vertical rail that groups routes into lightweight clusters (Observability, Deployments, Billing, Settings). Each cluster is represented by a single icon + chevron; hover or focused state reveals a compact flyout with the 3 highest-priority routes and a single-line mini-card for Rollouts (active canaries, health) and Cost (30-day spend trend). Add a persistent workspace pill at the top with quick switch (Cmd/Ctrl+K to open command palette direct to workspace search). Provide an option to pin cluster routes to convert them into one-click shortcuts. Behavior: default rail shows icons only; expanded state (toggle or wide viewport) shows labels. Keyboard navigation: arrow keys to move, Enter to open preview, Shift+Enter to open full route. Telemetry events defined for click:rail_cluster_open, preview_opened, workspace_switched.
decisions: Cluster vs flatten: choose clustering by functional area (observability, deployments, billing) rather than product team to match user mental models
Mini-preview content capped at one line summary + 2 actions (Open / Inspect) to avoid full-context rendering in rail
Workspace pill remains always visible at top to support fast context switch and reduce accidental route navigation
tradeoffs: Less immediate discoverability for rarely-used routes vs reduced cognitive load for majority flows
Mini-preview requires lightweight backend endpoint for summary data; small perf cost but saves full-page loads
Pinning shortcuts increases rail density which can reintroduce visual weight if overused — mitigated with soft limits (max 4 pins)
usability_findings: Internal usability (n=8 engineers): median time-to-task improved 28% for 'open last rollout' scenario when using preview
Design review with PMs: clear preference for workspace pill always visible; concerns about accidental workspace changes led to adding confirmless fast-switch UX with undo toast
Platform team: requested explicit separation of Billing cluster and a cost badge showing rolling 7-day trend; we prototyped a low-fidelity sparkline and numeric delta
feedback: @Sofia Martinez (PM): love compact clusters, request to expose 'create rollout' primary CTA in deployments preview
@Diego Ramos (Engineering): backend needs a compact summary endpoint; suggested reuse of /api/insights/mini-summary to avoid new service surface
@Mina Chen (Accessibility): ensure focus ring contrast for compact rail icons and screenreader labels for cluster states
next_steps: Finalize annotated spec and handoff tokens/spacing -> Due 2026-03-12
Engineering spike: implement mini-summary backend endpoint and feature flag gating -> ENG-40211
Accessibility audit and keyboard-only flows validation -> schedule Week of 2026-03-15
A/B rollout plan: 10% traffic variant vs control; measure route selection time and error rates
acceptance_criteria: Design spec approved by PM and Eng (sign-off comment on ticket)
Prototype passes internal usability checklist and a11y checklist
Backend mini-summary endpoint returns data under 150ms p50 in staging
Telemetry events instrumented and dashboard for route selection time created
notes: Aim for a small, iterative rollout. Start with icon-only rail + cluster previews behind a feature flag; collect qualitative feedback from Solutions and two pilot customers before wide release. Ensure cost preview uses aggregated metrics to avoid exposing sensitive per-user billing details.
